Imagine having an idea for an app but not knowing how to code. Until recently, you’d probably need a developer or an entire team to bring it to life.

That’s starting to change.

With Abacus.AI Agent, you can turn a simple text prompt into a working product, from building apps to launching an online business.

Here are 8 things you can do with agent.abacus.ai/anj👇

🔥 Build and launch apps — Turn your idea into a live app without building everything from scratch.
🎮 Create mobile apps & 3D games — Bring your ideas to life with AI.
🚀 Build a one-person company — Create full-stack products, including complex personal finance apps.
💰 Launch an online business — Build a website with a database and Stripe payments.
📈 Create micro-SaaS products — Build tools like a subscription-based resume analyzer.
🔄 Clone apps and websites — Create your own CRM, Notion-style tool, or SaaS product.
💡 Turn an idea into a startup — Build fintech dashboards, budget trackers, and mobile apps using text prompts.
⚡ Find and fix bugs — Use AI agent swarms to work on glitches and coding issues in parallel.

The interesting part isn't just that AI can write code. It's that you can now go from an idea to a working product without having to do everything yourself.

You bring the idea. AI helps you build it.

11 min

Seguir

🎓 Excited to share that I've completed the Professional Certificate Program in Agentic AI and Applications by IITM Pravartak Technologies Foundation (Technology Innovation Hub of IIT Madras) and Emeritus!

This six-month journey was built almost entirely on weekends. While weekdays were busy with work, Saturdays and Sundays went into live sessions, hands-on labs, and a lot of trial and error to understand how AI agents think, plan, and act. Giving up weekends wasn't always easy, but it was absolutely worth it.

🔍 Key concepts I got familiar with:
•   Foundations: Python, APIs, and how LLMs work (tokens, embeddings, context windows, transformers)
•   Prompt engineering, Vector search and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to ground answers in real data
•    Agent workflows with LangChain and LangGraph: state, tools, and human-in-the-loop
•    Reasoning patterns like ReAct and reflection, plus multi-agent orchestration
•     Agent memory, context engineering, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
•     Evaluation, guardrails, and responsible AI: hallucination detection and prompt injection

🛠️ Capstone: AI Support Resolution Agent (LangChain) : A project that brought six months of learning together, built in phases:
•    A baseline agent, then integrated with an LLM
•    RAG over support documents using a vector database
•    Tool calling for order lookups and support tickets
•    Planning, memory, and feedback for multi-turn conversations
•    A LangChain backend deployed as a web app, with interaction logging

💡 Bringing this to OpenText
I'm enthusiastic about applying these insights to our growth and innovation framework at OpenText. With its AI-first strategy and the Aviator family of AI assistants, OpenText sits where agentic AI creates the most value: on top of trusted enterprise content. Areas where I see these concepts fitting in:
•        RAG and enterprise search: grounding AI answers in governed, secure content so customers find what they need faster
•        Agentic workflows across content, service management, and business processes
•        Process and service automation, with escalation tEdito humans when needed
•        Developer and testing productivity: speeding up coding, testing, and backlog management
•        Responsible AI for sensitive enterprise data

Looking forward to putting these skills into practice at OpenText. A big thank you to the faculty, mentors, and fellow learners! 🙏
